title: A Computer That Learns From Old Storms Guessed Right
summary: When the first hurricane of this Atlantic season formed, a computer that learns from history did a better job than older models at guessing where it would go. In early October, Hurricane Isaias came ashore near Destin, Florida, as a Category 2 storm. Older models first said it would go farther west, toward southeastern Louisiana. But Google DeepMind's artificial intelligence model got it right from the start: it would hit the western Florida Panhandle. Meteorologist Michael Lowry calls DeepMind the gold standard model. He says it has been by far the best computer model forecasters have ever seen. Old models use live data and hard math to work out a storm's path and strength. The new AI model looks for patterns in thousands of old storms. The Hurricane Center still mixes several models together, and people read the results before telling the public.
why_it_matters: Better storm predictions help families know when to stay safe or leave home before a hurricane arrives.
